Project fit

Refresh Your Home's Exterior With Professional Painting Solutions

A quality exterior paint job protects your home and dramatically improves curb appeal. RT Signature Homes reads the surface and the weather first, so preparation and coating choices refresh siding, trim, and doors with durable finishes built for Pacific Northwest conditions.

Typical scope

  • Surface-condition and coating review
  • Cleaning, scraping, sanding, repair, caulking, and priming
  • Siding, trim, doors, soffits, and compatible exterior elements
  • Color and coating-system coordination
  • Access, protection, weather windows, application, and cure planning

Why choose us

Why Choose Us for Our Exterior Painting Services

Preparation that lasts

An exterior painting project lasts only as long as its preparation, so we repair substrates and address moisture before any paint is applied.

Coordinated color

Siding, trim, doors, and architectural details are coordinated so color choices strengthen the house rather than flatten its character.

Built around the weather

We plan around weather and surface condition, which protects the finish and keeps the work from being redone a few seasons later.

Surface preparation

Prepare Exterior Surfaces Properly for Durable and Consistent Paint Finishes

Durable exterior results depend on thorough preparation, so peeling, failed joints, exposed substrate, mildew, and moisture issues are addressed before any coating is applied.

Preparation varies by material, with wood, stucco, and siding each needing the appropriate cleaning, scraping, sanding, or repairs to help new paint adhere and last.

Finished envelope

Protect Exterior Siding With Suitable Paints and Surface Treatments

The right coating system does more than add color; it protects siding and trim from moisture, UV, and seasonal weather.

We match compatible, weather-resistant products to each surface and plan scheduling around temperature, moisture, shade, and cure requirements so the finish performs over the long term.

Design and pre-construction

Construction and completion

The work is sequenced, protected, inspected, communicated, and closed out with a final walkthrough and documented completion items.

Budget and schedule orientation

Useful early guidance identifies what changes the investment and timeline. A responsible project range follows an assessment of the property, scope, finish expectations, and delivery constraints.

Questions homeowners ask

Exterior Painting FAQs

How can I tell whether my home's exterior needs repainting or surface repairs first?

Peeling paint, cracked coatings, exposed wood, bubbling, and persistent discoloration can indicate that preparation or repairs are needed. Damaged siding, deteriorated trim, and moisture intrusion should be evaluated before repainting so the underlying problems are addressed rather than covered.

Does exterior painting require different preparation for wood, stucco, and siding?

Yes, each material requires appropriate preparation. Wood may need scraping and sanding, stucco may require crack repairs and compatible coatings, and siding needs cleaning and an assessment of its existing finish. The preparation method should match the surface condition and paint manufacturer's recommendations.

How do I choose exterior paint colors that work with my roof and existing materials?

Start with fixed features such as roofing, brick, stone, and other materials that will remain unchanged. Choose a main exterior color that complements those features, then select coordinating trim and accent colors. Testing samples in different lighting conditions can help you evaluate the final combination.

Why is exterior paint peeling even when the surface was painted recently?

Peeling can occur when paint is applied over dirty or damp surfaces, incompatible coatings, loose existing paint, or improperly prepared materials. Moisture problems can also cause coating failure. Identifying the cause and correcting it before repainting helps reduce the chance of recurring peeling.

What weather conditions are suitable for exterior painting?

Exterior painting generally requires suitable temperatures, manageable humidity, and surfaces that are dry. Rain, heavy dew, direct intense sunlight, or strong winds can affect application and drying. The product manufacturer's temperature and weather guidelines should be followed for the specific paint being used.
